title: Vendor Pseudonymization & Ephemeral Logs Addendum (Template)
summary: Template addendum to be attached to vendor agreements when the vendor will process or route customer prompt/usage data. Focuses on pseudonymization techniques, ephemeral logging controls, evidence and audit obligations, and narrow exceptions for troubleshooting.
content:
Purpose: This addendum supplements the main agreement between [CUSTOMER] and [VENDOR] (together, the Parties) and sets out requirements specific to pseudonymization of customer-originated data and ephemeral logging practices used by the Vendor in connection with services that process natural language inputs, model prompts, embeddings, or other potentially sensitive textual content.

1. Definitions
- Pseudonymization: The technical processing of personal data such that it can no longer be attributed to a specific data subject without the use of additional information which is kept separately and subject to technical and organizational measures.
- Ephemeral Logs: Operational and telemetry logs that are time-limited and stored only for a defined short retention window intended for immediate troubleshooting, monitoring, or short-term analytics, after which they are deleted or irreversibly transformed.
- Material Customer Data: Any data provided by or on behalf of the Customer, including prompts, attachments, outputs, and metadata, that could reasonably contain personal data or confidential business information.

2. Core Obligations of the Vendor
2.1 Pseudonymization by Default: Except where prohibited by law or necessary to perform the Services, the Vendor shall pseudonymize Material Customer Data at the earliest practicable point in the vendor’s processing pipeline. Pseudonymization techniques should aim to remove or replace direct identifiers (names, email addresses, account IDs) and, where feasible, deterministic or reversible identifiers.
2.2 Minimal Metadata: The Vendor shall avoid capturing persistent identifiers or long-lived correlation tokens in telemetry tied to Material Customer Data. When correlation is required for operational reasons, correlation keys must be ephemeral and rotated at intervals no longer than 12 hours unless otherwise agreed in writing.
2.3 Ephemeral Logging Windows: Operational logs that include any Material Customer Data or fragments thereof must be retained only for a maximum of 72 hours by default. Where operational needs require longer retention (for example, extended forensic investigations), the Vendor may retain logs for up to 30 days only after: (i) providing written notice to the Customer describing the scope, purpose, and specific data elements; and (ii) obtaining Customer approval which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
2.4 Secure Storage & Encryption: While persisting any logs or pseudonymization mapping tables, the Vendor must encrypt data at rest and in transit using industry-standard algorithms (e.g., AES-256 for at-rest, TLS 1.2+ for transit). Key management must be documented and limited to authorized personnel.

3. Mapping Tables and Re-identification Controls
3.1 Mapping Table Minimization: If the Vendor maintains mapping tables to permit re-association of pseudonymized tokens to original identifiers, those mapping tables must be stored separately from the pseudonymized dataset, access-controlled, and retained for no longer than 90 days unless otherwise approved by the Customer.
3.2 Access Governance: Access to mapping tables or any re-identification mechanisms must be limited to named individuals with a documented business justification. Vendor shall provide an access log of any re-identification events on a quarterly basis and upon reasonable Customer request within 10 business days.

4. Logging Redaction & Data Masking
4.1 Automatic Redaction: Vendor shall implement automated redaction filters in logging pipelines to remove sequences resembling high-risk identifiers (e.g., social security numbers, credit card numbers, API keys) before logs are written to persistent storage.
4.2 Manual Review Controls: Any manual review of logs that contain Material Customer Data must occur in an access-controlled environment with multi-factor authentication and must be limited to the minimum number of staff necessary. Manual review sessions must be logged and retained for 180 days.

5. Exception Handling and Troubleshooting
5.1 Controlled Exceptions: For critical production incidents where pseudonymized data prevents effective diagnosis, the Vendor may request a temporary exception to access fully-identifiable data. Such requests must be made in writing to the Customer’s security contact, specifying the scope, duration (no more than 7 days), personnel, and steps to be taken to minimize exposure.
5.2 Post-Incident Review: Following any exception, the Vendor shall produce a post-incident report that includes the root cause, the specific data elements accessed, remedial steps, and confirmation that any retained forensic artifacts were deleted or further pseudonymized.

6. Evidence, Audit Rights & Reporting
6.1 Attestation: The Vendor will provide a quarterly attestation confirming compliance with the retention windows and pseudonymization commitments in this Addendum.
6.2 Audit Rights: The Customer shall have the right to request an annual remote technical audit limited to controls relevant to pseudonymization, ephemeral logging, and access governance. On-site audits may be requested no more than once per 24 months and require reasonable notice. Vendor may redact unrelated material but may not deny reasonable inspection of controls or evidence.
6.3 Breach Notification: In the event that logs or mapping tables containing Material Customer Data are accessed or disclosed in violation of this Addendum, Vendor shall notify the Customer within 48 hours of detection with the information reasonably available at the time.

7. Subprocessors & Flow-Down
7.1 Subprocessor Requirements: Prior to engaging subprocessors that will process Material Customer Data or Ephemeral Logs, Vendor must: (i) notify the Customer at least 30 days in advance; (ii) ensure subprocessors agree in writing to equivalent pseudonymization and ephemeral log controls; and (iii) remain liable for the subprocessors’ compliance.

8. Remedies & Limitations
8.1 Remedial Actions: Failure to comply with the core obligations may trigger remediation steps including mandatory remediation plans, independent verification, or suspension of data processing for the affected workloads if risk cannot be mitigated within a reasonable period.
8.2 No Excessive Liability: The Parties agree to apply the liability and limitation of liability provisions of the underlying Agreement to claims arising under this Addendum, except where local law requires otherwise.

9. Miscellaneous
9.1 Conflicts: If there is any conflict between this Addendum and the underlying Agreement, the terms of this Addendum shall govern only with respect to the topics expressly covered herein.
9.2 Amendment: This Addendum may be amended by written agreement of the Parties.

Appendix A – Suggested Pseudonymization Techniques and Examples
- Tokenization with per-customer salt and short-lived token TTLs.
- Format-preserving transformations for non-sensitive fields where structure must be preserved for processing.
- Hash + truncate + rotate: compute a keyed hash of identifier then truncate and rotate keys regularly.

Appendix B – Operational Checklist for Vendor Implementation (examples)
- Inventory of systems that receive Material Customer Data.
- Logging pipeline diagram with redaction points.
- List of encrypted storage locations and KMS configuration.
- Mapping table registry with retention schedule and access list.

Note to template users: This document is intended as a negotiable addendum. Specific retention windows, rotation schedules, and exception durations should be aligned with Customer’s risk profile and legal requirements. Always pair with the primary DPA clauses when Material Customer Data includes personal data subject to privacy laws.
